title: The CDC tells caregivers to talk, read, and sing to a 2-month-old
summary: A CDC tip for 2-month-olds is to talk, read, and sing to the baby to help language develop.
body: On the CDC 2-month tips, one line says to talk, read, and sing to your baby to help her develop and understand language. It is an activity for the adult, not a milestone the baby is expected to pass. The page does not measure how many minutes of reading change a later score. A 4-month tip uses similar words and adds that this helps the baby learn to speak and understand words later. Both lines are United States CDC suggestions.
